messages:
ashley-support: Heads up — customer 'Parkly' just opened a Sev about huge latency spikes and 502s. They say requests are being routed to `us-west-2` even though they pinned `eu-west-1` in the dashboard. They saw multiple short failovers.
jen.sre: ugh. any request ids or example timestamps?
ashley-support: gave us these request ids: r-33a2, r-33b9. Reported around 11:02–11:12 UTC. They say the app observed a fallback to us-west twice.
max.platform: Opsbot shows a deploy at 2026-03-17T09:50Z that touched healthcheck suppression logic (PR #4427). @opsbot can you paste the deploy marker?
opsbot: deploy: service/route-controller @max.platform deployed commit 8f3b2 on 2026-03-17T09:50:12Z — change: healthcheck suppression TTL refactor.
jen.sre: timeline fits. Healthcheck suppression could be mis-evaluating multi-region probes and suppressing eu checks, causing route controller to think eu is unhealthy and flip to us-west.
ashley-support: customer attached a screenshot of the routing table during the incident showing eu backend marked degraded.
lucy-ml: I can repro locally — if probe responses are slightly delayed the new logic marks the origin as suppressed for 30s instead of 3s. Looks like TTL got set to milliseconds -> seconds regression.
oncall-sre: Can someone run a quick check against staging? Also need logs from the route controller for the two request ids.
jen.sre: grabbing logs:
```
$ grep -E "r-33a2|r-33b9" /var/logs/route-controller/2026-03-17.log | tail -n 50
2026-03-17T09:51:11Z route-controller route=eu-west-1 state=degraded reason=probe_timeout suppress_until=2026-03-17T09:51:41Z
2026-03-17T09:51:12Z route-controller route=eu-west-1 state=unhealthy reason=probe_fail
2026-03-17T09:51:42Z route-controller route=eu-west-1 state=healthy reason=probe_success
```
jen.sre: suppression window shows 30s. expected 3s.
max.platform: ok rollback PR queued for the suppression TTL refactor. Rolling back to previous commit 5d2aa.
ashley-support: customer is asking for a timeline and whether billing/regression impacted. They saw increased token usage due to retries.
lucy-ml: repro steps for SRE playbook:
```
1) curl -v https://health.redwood.net/probe?region=eu-west-1 -H 'X-Test-Probe: true' --limit-rate 1k
2) simulate 150ms delay on probe responder (iptables tc)
3) observe route-controller logs for `suppress_until` values
```
oncall-sre: I applied the rollback at 09:58Z. route-controller restarted and now suppression TTL is back to 3s. opsbot, can you confirm health metrics?
opsbot: metric: route-controller.suppression_ttl (avg) before=29.7s after=3.0s.
jen.sre: customer notified and support confirmed traffic routed back to eu-west-1 around 09:59Z.
ashley-support: customer replies: latency back to normal, appreciated the quick fix. They asked for a postmortem.
max.platform: creating a postmortem draft and linking PR/commit. Action items: revert the refactor branch tests, add e2e for multi-region suppression, and add an alert if suppression_ttl > 10s.
oncall-sre: also add instrumentation so routing decisions include the probe response timestamps in traces.
ashley-support: adding follow-up notes to the ticket about potential billing impact (retries).
jen.sre: closing loop — will schedule a short blameless postmortem review at 14:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
